title: Dark Chocolate Sorbet
changes_from_base: Dark chocolate and cocoa simmered with water and sugar replace the fruit; corn syrup keeps it scoopable.
summary: Intensely chocolatey with no cream or milk: cocoa and dark chocolate simmered with water make a silky, deep sorbet.

ingredients.item: light corn syrup or glucose syrup
fine sea salt or table salt
dark chocolate (about 70%), finely chopped; check the label for milk

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Whisk the water, cocoa, sugar, corn syrup and salt in the pan and bring to the boil, whisking.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Turn the heat right down and let it barely bubble for 5 min, stirring all the time so it does not catch.

steps.title: Melt
steps.text: Take it off the heat, add the chocolate and vanilla and whisk until smooth and glossy.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Pass it through the sieve into the bowl set in iced water and stir now and then until it is cold. Cover and refrigerate for 4 h or more.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Stir well, churn for 20-25 min until it looks like a thick milkshake, then freeze for at least 2 h. It is best within 5 days.

tips: Use a good dark chocolate you like eating; its flavour is the whole dessert.
Keep the heat low while simmering, as cocoa catches easily.
A pinch of flaky salt or a few raspberries on top is all it needs.
storage: Keep covered in the freezer for up to 5 days. Soften for 10 min before scooping.
